From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Zephyr ��������post-call recap & a few integration questions

Hi Alex / Sarah �

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and a few follow-ups so your engineering team can evaluate integration effort: 

Recap (2 bullets):
- Primary use case: hybrid chat assistant for customer support + a daily analytics reranker that pre-sorts docs for search.
- Volume expectation: low latency for chat (p95 < 300ms), batch embedding/rerank jobs ~200k docs/day to start.

Integration questions (please confirm preferred options / constraints):
1) SDK & auth: We provide language SDKs (Python/Node/Go). For sensitive data you can use token-based API keys or customer-managed mTLS + KMS. Which auth mode does Zephyr prefer? Any IP allowlist or proxy requirements?
2) Routing & fallbacks: Do you want routing by region vs latency tiers? Should we include an automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant if the primary model is unavailable?
3) Structured output / tool-calling: For the chat assistant you mentioned calling internal tools (ticket create, run query). Are you expecting structured JSON outputs (tool schema) or just text prompts? Do you plan to use our function/tool-calling primitives?
4) Embeddings & reranker: Please confirm the canonical document ID field and whether you need versioning metadata returned with embeddings. Also, expected embedding dimensionality tolerance (we support 1536/1024/768 etc).
5) Request/response schema (RSP): A couple of quick clarifications we need to recommend correct request shapes: chat vs completions, tokenization & max_tokens limits (are you expecting long context > 32k tokens?), stop token behavior, streaming semantics (do you need token-by-token streaming for UI?).

Attachments: I attached a sample network diagram and initial RSP schema we recommend.

Next steps / asks:
- If you can confirm (1) auth mode and (2) whether you'll use function/tool-calling by Mon, our eng team will produce a short integration plan and sample SDK snippet.
- If you can share a sample doc and expected responses for the reranker, Dev will run a quick local eval with our embeddings.

Thanks —Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zephyr.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@zephyr.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Apr 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zephyr ��������� �post-call recap & a few integration questions

Thanks Marissa �— great summary. Answers inline below.

1) SDK & auth: We prefer API key + mTLS for the control plane. We can provide IP ranges for an allowlist if needed. KMS integration will be used for long-term secrets.

2) Routing & fallbacks: Region-level routing (us-east primary) is fine. Yes, automatic fallback to a quantized variant would be helpful for heavy load. We care about deterministic fallbacks (same model family).

3) Structured output / tool-calling: We want to adopt function/tool-calling for ticket creation and entity extraction. Prefer strict JSON tool responses so downstream systems can parse reliably.

4) Embeddings & reranker: We'll use doc_id (string) as canonical id. Versioning should be returned as metadata. Start with 1536-dim embeddings. We will send batches of ~5k docs for the initial sync.

5) RSP specifics:
- Chat vs completions: For the assistant UI we'll use chat for system + multi-turn context, but for the reranker & some bulk transforms we'll call the completion endpoint to get deterministic single-turn outputs.
- Tokenization & max_tokens: We'll likely need up to 64k token context for a subset of analytic workflows. Can you confirm model/context limits and tokenization scheme?
- Stop tokens: We want explicit stop sequences when invoking tools. Also confirm behavior when both stop tokens and max_tokens are hit.
- Streaming: Need token-by-token streaming for the agent UI. Also want partial function-call streaming (i.e., stream arguments as they are generated) if possible.

Attachments: attaching a sample doc export and a short internal requirements doc.

Happy to hop on a quick call with Dev and Dylan if that helps.

�����—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Zephyr Analytics
alex.chen@zephyr.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zephyr.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zephyr �������� ��post-call recap & a few integration questions

Hi Alex �

thanks for the details. A few technical clarifications from our side and what we can provide out-of-the-box: 

- Auth: API key + mTLS is supported. We can also support customer-managed KMS for key rotation. If you can send IP ranges we will add them to the allowlist.

- Region & fallback: We can route by latency/region and provide an ordered fallback list. For deterministic fallbacks we'll pin to the same model family and expose the variant name in responses (metadata.model_variant).

- Function/tool-calling & structured output: Our SDK supports OpenAI-style function calling. We return a structured JSON envelope: {"type":"tool_call","name":"create_ticket","arguments":{...}} when a tool is invoked. (Note: quoted here for clarity; full machine-readable schema attached as rsp_schema_v1.json). We also support content-type negotiation and strict schema validation on our side if you want us to enforce shapes pre-dispatch.

- Embeddings: We support 1536-dim vectors. Our bulk ingestion accepts gzip'ed ndjson batched payloads. We will return document metadata including version, doc_id, and last_modified in the ingestion response.

- Context size & tokenization: Current public models we recommend support up to 32768 tokens; we have private variants that can go to 65k+ depending on model family and memory profile. Tokenization is BPE-based using the same tokenizer as the model (we'll report token counts in the SDK helper). If you expect 64k contexts for specific analytics jobs, we should schedule an architecture sync to pick an appropriate model shard/variant.

- max_tokens & stop behavior: If both stop sequences and max_tokens are provided, our runtime will stop on the first event (either a stop match or reaching max_tokens). We'll return a metadata.reason field: "stop_token" or "max_tokens".

- Streaming & partial tool streaming: We stream tokens by default for streaming-enabled endpoints. Partial tool-call argument streaming is supported as an opt-in mode (streaming.function_args=true). We'll note that some SDKs buffer by default; we'll provide example snippets to enable streaming in the UI clients.

Attached: rsp_schema_v1.json with the envelope shapes, function definitions for create_ticket and extract_entities, and example request/response sequences.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa / Dylan: share the example UI flow you want streamed (a short video or sequence) so we can validate latency expectations.
- Alex: confirm IP ranges and whether you want strict schema validation pre-dispatch.

Happy to join a call today at 2pm PT if that works.

�—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Runtime Integrations | Redwood Inference
